message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  

**What you can do instead:**

| Source | How to use it | Typical info it gives |
|--------|---------------|-----------------------|
| **AirNow.gov** (U.S. EPA) | Go to the website, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and click “Get AQI.” | Current AQI value, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, O₃, NO₂, etc.), health advisories. |
| **AQICN.org** | Search “Los Angeles” or use the mobile app. | Global AQI index, forecast, historical trends. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Look for “air quality” or “smog” sections. | Often include short‑term forecasts and health tips. |
| **Weather apps** (Weather.com, AccuWeather, Weather Underground) | Check the “Air Quality” tab. | Usually shows AQI and pollutant levels. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities or have respiratory concerns, it’s best to check one of those sources right now. If you’d like a quick example of what an AQI reading might look like, let me know!
